Dear Wanderer, as I write these words, I hope they find you well.
Some time ago, I accompanied the Prefect on an inspection of the local school. There, I saw the children sitting upright with solemn faces, buried in their books—so engrossed they didn’t even notice our approach.
Curious, I wondered what marvelous texts could captivate these usually restless youngsters so completely. Upon asking, I learned they were reading books you had gifted them not long ago.
When I inquired what made these books special, the children eagerly chimed in, and I realized you had thoughtfully chosen a different book for each child. Hearing that I knew you, they begged me to pass on their gratitude.
Yet, when pressed to articulate their thanks, the little ones grew shy and tongue-tied. So, I suggested they write down their thoughts, and here they are, sealed within this letter—though I swear I didn’t peek!
Oh, and the children also entrusted me with a few drawings, inspired by the books you gave. They insisted you, of all people, would appreciate their "masterpieces," as they called them, for having the finest taste.
Ha Ha, it seems if there’s ever a task involving children in the future, you’re the one to turn to.
